overview.description: Professionals call plasmids 'backbones' and match the backbone to the situation. For a first project, pick a simple plasmid with high copy number and an easy-to-source antibiotic - e.g. pET-15b or an iGEM pSB1C3.
objectives: select a backbone by copy number, resistance and MCS
match a backbone to your expression goal
find and download sequences from Addgene

instructions.title: List requirements
instructions.description: Decide copy number, resistance marker, promoter and whether you need an affinity tag.

instructions.title: Shortlist backbones
instructions.description: Compare candidates (pET-15b, pSB1C3, etc.) against your requirements.

instructions.title: Download the sequence
instructions.description: Pull the annotated .dna/.gb file from Addgene for in-silico design.

submission.description: Choose a backbone, justify it against your requirements, and attach the annotated sequence file.
